questions.question: 144. A 29-year-old female presents to her GP. She has noticed dandruff and a rash on her face. On examination there is evidence of areas of erythema with fine scaling over her nasal bridge, around her nasolabial fold and eyebrows and ears and there is evidence of fine Scaling on the scalp. Given the most likely diagnosis, which of the following organisms may be associated?
questions.explanation: 144... The answer is A. The clinical features described are characteristic of Seborrhoeic dermatitis. It is thought to be caused by an inflammatory reaction to the yeast Malassezia Typically the face and scalps is affected as described here however other areas which can be involved include the sternum and upper back and the skin flexures. Treatment includes topical ketoconazole including shampoo and topical steroids intermittently. More severe disease may be treated with oral antifungals and UV light treatment.

questions.question: 145. A 27-year-old soldier has just returned from Afghanistan. He has been sent to the dermatology due to a lesion on his right forearm. He states that this began as a small red patch which them increased in size. On examination there is an erythematous raised lesion on his right forearm which has ulcerated and has crusted over. He is otherwise well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 145... The answer is C. Given where the patient has travelled to and the description of the lesion, the most likely diagnosis is cutaneous leishmaniasis. Cutaneous Leishmaniasis is caused by old world protozoa such as L. tropica or Infantum or new world protozoa such as L. Mexicana. This leads to the lesion described. Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis is a risk in new world leishmaniasis. Visceral leishmaniasis is caused by L. Donovani or Chagasi and affects the reticuloendothelial system and leads to anaemia and hepatosplenomegaly.

questions.question: 146. A 28-year-old soldier presents with an itchy rash. He is itchy in his finger webs, wrists and groin and there is evidence of excoriation in these areas. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 146... The answer is B. The history is indicative of scabies. AS well as the wrist, finger webs and groin other areas commonly affected are elbows and perineum. Sometimes burrow holes can be observed and mites extracted with a needle. The whole body must be treated with topical preparations such as gamma benzene hexachloride or benzyl benzoate Due to the lack of the classical rashes in the other diagnoses and the areas affected the other diagnoses are less likely.

questions.question: 147. A 60-year-old gentleman presents with a mole on the sole of his foot. On examination there is evidence of a 1.5cm mole with border irregularity and a halo surrounding it. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 147... The answer is C. The most likely diagnosis is acral lentiginous melanoma which is observed on the sole of the foot. It is often surrounded by a halo of paler skin. Periungual melanoma is not the diagnosis as it occurs in the nail bed. Lentigo maligna melanoma is a large flat area of pigmentation. Nodular melanoma is very aggressive and is nodular and can be depigmented and does not occur on the sole.

questions.question: 148. A patient with ulcerative colitis develops several necrotic ulcers on her legs. How do you manage these?
options: D- Local application of silver nitrate
questions.explanation: 148... The answer is C. The likely diagnosis is pyoderma gangrenosum and prednisolone is the most appropriate from this list for management.

questions.question: 149. A 37-year-old male notices a blistering rash on his hands developing after worting on a sunny day in the garden. This has occurred previously and led to some scarring. He hag yso noticed some hait developing on his cheek. What investigation would you perform
questions.explanation: 149... The answer is C. The most likely diagnosis is porphyria cutanea tarda (deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase leading to uroporphyrinogen III, accumulation). It can be inherited or secondary to alcohol related liver disease. It leads to blister formation and scarring, hypertrichosis in face and scarring alopecia in severe. It is confirmed by increased plasma  and urinary uroporphyrins.

questions.question: 150.A 28-year-old soldier presents with an itchy rash. He is itchy in his finger webs, writs and groin and there is evidence of excoriation in these areas. What is the most likehy diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 150... The answer is B. The history is indicative of scabies. AS well as the wrist, finger webs and groin other areas commonly affected are elbows and perineum. Sometimey burrow holes can be observed and mites extracted with a needle. The whole body must be freated with topical preparations such as gamma-benzene hexachloride or benzyl benzoate Due to the lack of the classical rashes in the other diagnoses and the areas affected the other diagnoses are less likely.

questions.question: 151. A 35-year-old presents with red scaly patches on her face, scalp and hands. On examination there is evidence of red plaques on her face, hands and scalp with some bald patches. Some of the patches are scarring and discoloured. What is the diagnosis that fits best with this clinical picture?
questions.explanation: 151... The answer is C. The most likely diagnosis is CDLE. It leads to scaly, erythematous plaques on sun exposed areas. It is a chronic disease, relapsing and remitting and eventually the plaques atrophy and scar, undergo pigment change and lead to telangiectasia. It is treated with sun block and steroids. Psoriasis does not lead to the scarring and pigment change. Similarly neither does seborrheic dermatitis and does not lead to plaques.

questions.question: 152. A 14-year-old girl presents with moderate acne and pustules affecting the face, back and chest. How would you manage this case?
options: A- Oral tetracycline for three months
questions.explanation: 152... The answer is A. Due to the fact this patient has features of moderate acne then oral tetracycline for three months is the most appropriate treatment. Erythromycin is an altermative. This is a second line treatment and mild acne is normally treated with topical agents such as topical antibiotics, keratolytics or topical retinoids. Dianette is another option but is also used as a contraceptive and has other implications. Roaccutane is an oral retinoid and is a third line therapy only prescribed by dermatologists and with certain inclusion criteria due to the teratogenicity.

questions.question: 153. A 52 year old with known alcohol excess presents with facial flushing, pustules and telangiectasia predominantly around the nose. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 153... The answer is E. Rosacea leads to the symptoms described. Due to the increased reactivity of the facial vasculature there is facial flushing. It leads to erythema.,telangiectasia and acneiform lesions especially around the nose, cheeks and chin.Rhinophyma can occur where there is enlargement of the nose due to follicular entargement and although rosacea is more common in females this variant is more commonly seen in men. Blepharitis may also be associated. Sunlight, heat, alcohol and certain foods worsen the appearance. Acne leads to comedo (black head) formation and not facial flushing and is unlikely in a patient this age. Seborrhoeic dermatitis leads to greasy scales and often affects the scalp and different distribution and does not leads to the features described. The main treatment for rosacea is to avoid triggering factors, oxytetracycline and retinoids in severe cases. Topical steroids can lead to severe worsening of erythema.

questions.question: 154. A 72-year-old female presents to her GP after noticing blisters on her arms and legs She has recently been commenced on furosemide. On examination there is tense blister evident predominantly on the flexural surfaces of her arms and legs. There is no evidence of blisters in her mucous membranes. There is some healing areas where the blisters have burst but no evidence of scarring. A skin biopsy is organized and reveals subepidermal blister and inflammatory infiltrate with numerous eosinophils. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 154... The answer is D. The most likely diagnosis is Bullous pemphigoid which leads to the clinical findings above. In comparison to Pemphigus which often presents the mucous membranes and leads to superficial blisters, easily ruptured and with an intradermal pattern.Furosemide, NSAIDs and ACE inhibitors and penicillamine can lead to the development of pemphigoid. Bullous pemphigoid is an autoimmune disorder which leads to autoantibody formation to hemidesmosome proteins (attach basal cell to basement membrane). This leads to a split between epidermis and dermis and thus tense blister formation. There is no history of eczema and herpes does not cause large tense blisters. Dermatitis herpetiformis is usually on the extensor surfaces and there is often a history of Coeliac.

questions.question: 155. A 22-year-old female with some bowel habit change presents with a rash on her buttocks, elbows and knees. It is erythematous with some blistering and it is intensely itchy,A skin biopsy reveals sub-epidermal blister formation and immunofluorescence reveals IgA present within the papillae. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy for her?
questions.explanation: 155... The answer is E. The clinical findings and skin biopsy makes the likely diagnosis dermatitis herpetiformis which occurs often in the context of coeliac disease. It responds like coeliac to a gluten free diet. Dapsone can be used if the symptoms do not resolve.

questions.question: 156. A 27-year-old female who works in a nursing home is referred to the clinic with an itchy rash on her hands. On examination her hands are excoriated with some bleeding points and there is an erythematous papular rash on both hands with some vesicles. On patch testing, she is positive for latex. How would you manage this patient long term?
questions.explanation: 156... The answer is C. This patient has contact allergy to latex and allergen avoidance is the best long term management. Topical steroids, oral steroids and topical tacrolimus are useful in the short term to control symptoms.

questions.question: 157. A 50-year-old male who is a heavy smoker presents with velvety, hyperpigmented skin in his axillae. He has also noticed he has lost several stones in weight and has anorexia.What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 157... The answer is B. The rash described is typical of Acanthosis nigricans which is associated with Diabetes Mellitus, Obesity and Gastric Cancer. The history in this case is indicative of a gastric cancer.

questions.question: 158. A 22 year old female with some bowel habit change presents with a rash on her buttocks, elbows and knees. It is erythematous with some blistering and it is intensely itchy.A skin biopsy reveals sub-epidermal blister formation and immunofluorescence reveals IgA present within the papillae. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 158... The answer is B. The clinical findings and skin biopsy makes the likely diagnosis dermatitis herpetiformis which occurs often in the context of coeliac disease. It responds like coeliac to a gluten free diet. Dapsone can be used if the symptoms do not resolve. The skin biopsy findings are not in keeping with the other diagnoses.

questions.question: 159. A 23-year-old presents with yellow, brownish depressed patches on her shin. It began s a reddish brown color and new patches appear if she bumps her leg. She is also complaining of weight loss, polydipsia and polyuria. Which test should be performed?
questions.explanation: 159... The answer is E. This is a classical description of necrobiosis lipoidica which is associated with type I diabetes mellitus. It begins as erythematous patches, most commonly on the shin (but also face, scalp and arms) and then become yellow, depressed atrophic lesions. The Kobner phenomenon is seen. A fasting glucose should therefore be performed and treatment commenced.

questions.question: 160. A 55 year old female presents with a rash and she has noticed blisters forming. On examination she has areas of erythema and excoriations. She has dysuria. She is currently on atenolol and aspirin for hypertension. A skin biopsy is organized and shows intercellular staining of IgG on immunofluorescence. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 160... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is Pemphigus Vulgaris which is often Seen in middle aged patients. There s blister formation which are very friable unlike the tense subepidermal blisters in Bullous pemphigoid. It often affects the mucous membranes such as mouth or urethra. The skin biopsy results are also indicative. This can lead to odynophagia and dysuria. High dose steroids are required for management.

questions.question: 161. A 35-year-old man with inflammatory bowel disease presents with an ulcer. On examination he has a deep ulcerating lesion on his leg. How would you confirm the diagnosis?
options: A-Biopsy and culture from the ulcer
questions.explanation: 161... The answer is A. Pyoderma gangrenosum is a ulcerating disease which can occur with IBD. For diagnosis a biopsy and culture is required with a biopsy showing neutrophilic infiltration, haemorrhage and necrosis. Culture excludes infection. Steroids, both topical and oral have a role in management as does ciclosporin as a second line.

questions.question: 162. A 35-year-old gentleman presents to his GP with a firm ulcerated lesion of his nostril and nasal septum. He has just returned from travelling in South America. He is otherwise well. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 162... The answer is D. The history is indicative of Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis with the key being involvement of the nasal septum.

questions.question: 163. A patient with Ulcerative Colitis presents with problems with her stoma site. On examination there appears to be a large ulcer with a boggy necrotic base with erythema at its margins. It is very painful and she states it began as a pustule and it has been rapidly growing. Which of the following treatments should be commenced?
questions.explanation: 163... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is pyoderma gangrenosum. This can occur in the peristoma area. Oral steroids are the most effective treatment and should be utilized as they stop progression and prevents new lesions forming. Wound care and topical reatments such as steroids are also useful. Case reports also show success with mmunosupressants and biological therapies.

questions.question: 164. A 22-year-old male presents with left knee and right ankle pain and swelling. He has a rash on the palms of his hands and also on the soles of his feet. On examination of the hands there is hyperkeratotic waxy papules which have a yellow brown color. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 164... The answer is B. The skin lesions described are characteristic of keratoderma blennorrhagica which is a feature of reactive arthritis. Psoriatic arthritis affects small joints and does not lead to a yellow brown waxy appearance. There is no features suggestive of yphilis and there is normally a disseminated rash.

questions.question: 165. A 72-year-old female presents with a rash on her face. She states she had been unwell for a couple of days prior to the rash developing with malaise and fever and a few episodes of vomiting. On examination there is a bright fiery red, oedematous, warm, shiny area on the right side of her face, spreading from the paranasal area over the cheek, with borders which are sharply demarcated. This is painful, burning and itchy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 165... The answer is E. The history of preceding illness and the description of the rash is in keeping with Erysipelas. It is a superficial form of cellulitis, involving the dermis and upper gubcutaneous tissues. The most common causative agents are group A streptococci, group C and G. Strep. pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae have also been implicated. The patient is often unwell with a fever. The rash is painful, pruritic and tender and most commonly affects the face and legs. It tends to be unilateral but on the face can be symmetrical spreading from the paranasal area over the cheeks. It may follow a minor abrasion and the infection affects the superficial lymphatic vessels. It is differentiated from cellulitis as this is a deeper infection and the edges are not sharply demarcated like in erysipelas. In impetigo is a superficial infection and has a heavy honey coloured crust.

questions.question: 166.A 75 year old male presents with a lesion on the back of his hand. He states this has been increasing in size over the last few months. On examination there is evidence of an indurated hyperkeratotic nodule. The center has become necrotic and has begun to ulcerate and the edges are hard and raised. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 166... The answer is B. This is a typical description of a squamous cell carcinoma. It is a malignant tumor of keratinocytes. They are common on the hand, neck and backs of hands due to sun exposure. In immunosuppressed patient, these can become invasive. They can metastasise via the lymphatic system. Bowen's disease tends to be erythematous and scaly.BCC appear red, dome shaped nodules with a translucent appearance.

questions.question: 167. A 65 year old gentleman presents with a rapidly growing, solitary lesion near the lip. It has grown rapidly over the last few weeks. It is a nodule and the center is necrotic and crusted. You suspect this is a Keratoacanthoma. Which of the following is your next management step?
questions.explanation: 167... The answer is D. Keratoacanthoma is clinically and pathologically very difficult to distinguish from squamous cell carcinoma. On shave biopsy it is indistinguishable from squamous cell carcinoma. It is therefore recommended that any lesion suspected to be a keratoancanthoma be completely excised. Radiotherapy can be utilized for large lesions where excision may lead to cosmetic problems. Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen is utilized in the management of lesions such as actinic keratosis as is topical 5 fluorouracil.

questions.question: 168. A 30-year-old male presents with recurring painful genital ulcers and oral ulcers. He glso has a painful red eye and painful joints. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 168... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is Behcets syndrome which leads to recurrent orogenital ulceration. It can also lead to anterior uveitis and arthritis. Other less common features are abdominal pain and diarrhoea, aseptic meningitis and cranial nerve palsies. Reiters disease is characterized by urethritis, arthritis and conjunctivitis but does not lead to the ulceration described. Herpes simplex does not lead to arthritis. Similarly syphilis and Stevens Johnson are less likely to explain all the symptoms described.

questions.question: 169. A 37-year-old male notices a blistering rash on his hands developing after working on a sunny day in the garden. This has occurred previously and led to some scarring. He has also noticed some hair developing on his cheek. What investigation would you perform to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 169... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is porphyria cutanea tarda (deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase leading to uroporphyrinogen III, accumulation). It can be inherited or secondary to alcohol related liver disease. It leads to blister formation and scarring, hypertrichosis in face and scarring alopecia in severe. It is confirmed by increased plasma and urinary uroporphyrins.

questions.question: 170. A 68-year-old gentleman presents with a red, swollen, warm, hardened area of skin which is well demarcated and has a raised border. He is generally unwell with a fever.What organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: 170... The answer is C.The diagnosis is erysipelas. The most common causative agent ig Strep. pyogenes or also known as group A beta haemolytic strep. Other non A haemolytie

questions.question: 171. Which of the following best describes a solid, circumscribed elevation which is 7mm in diameter?
questions.explanation: 171... The answer is B. Nodules are solid, elevated lesions which are greater than 5mm and the greater part is beneath the skin. A papule is a small circumscribed elevated lesion. A pustule contains pus. A plaque is a flat topped palpable lesion and a macule is a flat lesion.

questions.question: 172. A 50-year-old female has recurrent problems with a troublesome tash. It is on her trunk and limbs and there is multiple lesions which are papular and itchy and she also hag some surrounding purpuric lesions. She is otherwise well. A biopsy is organized and reveals a lymphocytic vasculitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 172... The answer is A. Pityriasis lichenoides acuta is the most likely diagnosis. It is a cutaneous lymphocytic vasculitis where there is multiple crops of pruritic papules on the trunk and limbs and purpuric lesions are sometimes observed. It usually resolves spontaneously although topical treatments such as Ichthyol 1 percent. The other diagnoseg do not fit with the history and are not normally associated with purpuric lesions.

questions.question: 173. A 23-year-old male presents to his GP with painful penile ulcers. They have developed on his return from a safari where he had had unprotected sex. On examination, there is ulcers on his penis and he has suppurating groin lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 173... The answer is B. Chancroid is the most likely diagnosis. It is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi and is endemic in Africa. It begins as an erythematous papule which then forms a painful ulcers and sometimes several ulcers merge. Inguinal lymphadenopathy, usually unilaterally, can occur and suppurate. The other diagnoses can lead to similar features although herpes is unlikely to cause suppurative lymphadenopathy, however Chancroid is most likely due to his return from Africa.

questions.question: 174. How would you manage necrobiosis lipoidica?
questions.explanation: 174... The answer is E. Necrobiosis lipoidica can complicate diabetes mellitus, and is thought to lead to small vessel damage and partial necrosis of connective tissue. Support bandaging is utilised and low dose aspirin has been shown to aid healing.

questions.question: 175. A 21-year-old female presents to her GP after developing an intensely itchy erythematous rash around a new henna tattoo with vesicles present. What chemical is present in henna which led to this?
questions.explanation: 175... The answer is A. p.Phenylenediamine is the most likely culprit, being present in numerous hair dyes and henna tattoos. It can lead to an allergic dermatitis.

questions.question: 176. A 20-year-old present with diarrhoea, weight loss and an itchy rash on her scalp elbows and buttocks. You suspect dermatitis herpetiformis. On a skin biopsy. what Immunoglobulins is likely to be found on immunofluorescence?
questions.explanation: 176... The answer is D. In dermatitis herpetiformis, there is formation of subepidermal blisters and IgA deposits are found within the dermal papillae.

questions.question: 177. A 40-year-old female who has epilepsy has recently been started on a new drug, She has now developed a rash all over her body. There is evidence of large macules which are vety painful and also evidence where the epidermis has shed and there is dermis revealed This evident in the mouth also. She looks unwell and is pyrexial, tachycardie and hypotensive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 177... The answer is D. The most likely diagnosis is TEN. Phenytoin can lead to this and likely to be the culprit in this case. There may also be an eosinophilia or deranged LFTs. It can be life threatening due to massive fluid loss and superimposed infection. Stevens Johnson Syndrome is thought to be a milder form of TEN and predominantly effects the mucous membranes. Staphylococcal scalded syndrome tends to affect younger patients and forms multiple small blister and the epidermis is shed. Other causes of TEN include sulphonamides, nonsteroidal ant inflammatory drugs, allopurinol, methotrexate,antiretroviral drugs and corticosteroids as well as anticonvulsants. It may also complicate infection with Mycoplasma Pneumonia and Herpes.

questions.question: 178. A 30-year-old female presents to her GP with painful bruise like lesions on her shins.She has had a sore throat for the last few days. On examination there was evidence of red tender nodules and ankle swelling. What is the likely clinical outcome?
options: D- Will require Steroids for resolution
questions.explanation: 178... The answer is A. The diagnosis is erythema nodosum which normally resolves spontaneously. The most common causes are streptococcal infections (as in this case).sarcoidosis (often with bihilar lymphadenopathy), TB, IBD and Ankylosing Spondylitis.

questions.question: 179. A 24-year-old female who has previously self-harmed presents with a linear erythematous rash. What is most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 179... The answer is D. Rashes are not often linear and the history of self harm points towards a diagnosis of Dermatitis artefacta.

questions.question: 180. A 30 year old with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus presents with a painful erythematous papular rash with vesicles, predominantly on the scalp, buttocks and extensor surfaces. This has been ongoing for several months. A skin biopsy reveals subepidermal blister, papillary micro abscesses and infiltration of dermal papillae. How would you manage this patient?
options: C. Gluten free diet and dapsone
questions.explanation: 180...The answer is C. The diagnosis is dermatitis herpetiformis. As well as being associated with coeliac disease, it is also associated with other autoimmune disorders such as Type I DM and thyroid disease. A gluten free diet will aid with the rash and dapsone is wseful to resolve symptoms. Colchicine is also useful.

questions.question: 181. A 63-year-old female with pale complexion presents with an itchy pigmented lesion on her cheek. She had been burt several times as a child. On examination she has a 10mm dark flat lesion on her cheek. A skin biopsy confirms a melanoma in situ. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: A- Surgical excision 0.5cm surgical resection and chemotherapy
B- Surgical excision 1 cm resection margin
questions.explanation: 181... The answer is B. This patient has a lentigo maligna. Surgical excision is the treatment of choice with a resection margin of 1 cm recommended. Cryotherapy, radiotherapy and imiquimod cream are utilised if the patient is not fit for surgery. Chemotherapy is only utilised if there is metastases, this has a poor prognosis.

questions.question: 182. A patient presents with several areas of depigmented areas on his skin. They were scaly before depigmenting. There is no other symptoms. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: 182... The answer is A. The diagnosis is pityriasis versicolor it leads to patches of well demarcated scaling skin which then becomes depigmented. It is caused by a yeast thus treatment is usually with topical antifungals such as clotrimazole or terbinafine.

questions.question: 183. A 23 year old has been generally unwell with a fever and a painful facial rash which is getting progressively worse. The rash is erythematous, raised, indurated, tender and has a clear cut border. She is pyrexial and has a mild tachycardia. What organism is the likely culprit?
questions.explanation: 183... The answer is B. The diagnosis is erysipelas, most commonly caused by group A streptococcal infection. It leads to a superficial rapidly spreading erythematous skin rash with a well demarcated border and induration. Penicillin is the treatment of choice.

questions.question: 184. How would you investigate a patient with striated, rough, lustreless nails?
questions.explanation: 184...The answer is E. There is likely a fungal nail infection and this can be easily confirmed with a Woods Lamp which shows yellow/green fluorescence. Mycology is also useful for diagnosis but results take longer to return.

questions.question: 185. A 14-year-old girl presents with moderate acne and pustules affecting the face, back and chest. How would you manage this case?
questions.explanation: 185... The answer is E. Due to the fact this patient has features of moderate acne then oral tetracycline for three months is the most appropriate treatment. Erythromycin is an alternative. This is a second line treatment and mild acne is normally treated with topical agents such as topical antibiotics, keratolytics or topical retinoids. Dianette is another option but is also used as a contraceptive and has other implications. Roaccutane is an oral retinoid and is a third line therapy only prescribed by dermatologists and with certain inclusion criteria due to the teratogenicity.

questions.question: 186.A 72-year-old gentleman is referred to the clinic with a lesion on his cheek which has feen gradually increasing in size, is raised and has a pearly appearance with an ulcerated center. What of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 186... The answer is B. The slow growing papule or nodule on a sun exposed area is likely to be a BCC which can cause local erosion but very rarely metastasise. They appear as translucent or pearly lesions and have raised areas with telangiectasia and classically has an ulcerated center and indurated edge. It can cause significant destruction locally. Squamous cell carcinoma normally presents as an indurated nodular keratinizing or crusted lesion that may ulcerate, or may present as an ulcer without keratinization.

questions.question: 187. An 18-year-old girl presents in Autumn to her GP with a rash. She noticed a couple of weeks ago a small patch and several patches appeared and were itchy. On examination there was oval/ pink plaques on her trunk, upper arm and legs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 187... The answer is C. The most likely diagnosis is pityriasis rosea which is a self limiting rash mostly seen in young adults and that occurs most commonly in spring and autumn. The history and clinical findings are indicative and consist of circular or oval pink macules with a peripheral scale. It most often affects the trunk but can also involve the limbs. On the trunk it often follows a Christmas Tree pattern. Herpes virus 6 and 7 are thought to play a role. Lichen planus does not follow this pattern. In Guttate psoriasis although it can produce many small lesion son the trunk these tend to be salmon pink, less itchy and follow pharyngitis. SLE does not present in this manner. Some drugs can lead to a syndrome similar but there is no indication of this in the history.

questions.question: 188. A 20-year-old female presents with plaques at her scalp margins and on her knees. On examination there is evidence of hyperkeratotic plaques. Hair is sent for mycology and shows no growth. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 188... The answer is D. The most likely diagnosis is Psoriasis with the hyperkeratotic plaques and negative mycology excluding tinea capitis. The Kobner Phenomenon is a feature of psoriasis. The underlying pathology is increased skin turnover reflected by acanthosis and parakeratosis and there is a mixed neutrophilic and lymphohistiocytio perivascular infiltrate in the dermis.

questions.question: 189.A 25-year-old female with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes mellitus presents with several erythematous circular lesions on the dorsal aspect of her hand. The centre of the lesion is slightly depressed. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 189... The answer is D. Granuloma annulare is the most likely diagnosis, it can be associated with type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. It leads to small circular erythematous well circumscribed lesion with the centre sometimes being depressed or hyperpigmented and most often there is multiple lesions. They usually occur on the dorsum of the hands and feet. Necrobiosis lipoidica also occurs in patients with diabetes.

questions.question: 190. A 22 year old with Graves Disease presents as she has noticed some areas of depigmentation. She has just returned from holiday. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 190... The answer is A. The most likely diagnosis is vitiligo which leads to areas of skin depigmentation due to loss of melanocyte function. It is associated with autoimmune diseases. Leprosy does lead to depigmentation but these patches are also hypoaesthetic and should be considered depending on holiday destination. Chloasma is area of hyperpigmentation and pityriasis versicolor leads to discoloured patches.

questions.question: 191. A 22-year-old female with a history of Ulcerative colitis presents to the clinic with large painful ulcers on her legs, feels unwell and is feverish. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 191... The answer is E. Pyoderma gangrenosum is the most likely diagnosis with the history of large painful lesions of rapid onset and generally unwell and fever. It is associated with IBD and less commonly with RA and myeloma. This patient is young and very unlikely to have arterial or venous ulcers.

questions.question: 192. A 60-year-old male present to her GP with ulcers on his legs. He is a heavy smoker.On examination he has several punched out ulcers around the ankle and lower third of the shin. There is absence of the distal limb pulses. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 192... The answer is B. The most likely diagnosis is arterial ulcers due to the lack of distal pulses and history of heavy smoking. Venous ulcers often look heal thier and are sloughy and are often in the gaiter area of the legs and pulses are intact.

questions.question: 193. A 68 year old female who has previous had a DVT in her right leg presents to her GP with an ulcer. On examination there is an ulcer on the right leg just above the medial malleolus. It is sloughy and the surrounding skin is discoloured. Distal pulses are present.What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 193... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is a venous ulcer due to the history of a DVT, its location and distal pulses being present.

questions.question: 194. A 20-year-old female presents having noticed a hard area on her leg. On examination there is a small area of skin which is pale, indurated and appears glazed. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 194... The answer is D. Morphoea is the most likely diagnosis. It is characterised by a firm.white or violaceous patch of skin which can occur anywhere on the body but often on thighs, trunk and upper arms. The lesions when developing have a red or violet edge and then this fades and the lesion looks atrophic and glazed and is firm. The may be associated with Borrelia.

questions.question: 195. A 32-year-old female presents with a bald patch. It has been gradually increasing in size and is itchy and on examination it is scaling. A Woods Lamp reveals bright green immunofluorescence. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 195... The answer is C. The most likely diagnosis is Tinea capitis which is most often caused by T. Tonsurans, M. Canis, T. Rubrum or T. Verrucosum dermatophyte infection.M. Canis fluoresces green under a Woods light. It is treated with topical miconazole or ketoconazole. Psoriasis can lead to scaling and hair loss but would not fluoresce under a Woods light. Alopecia is not itchy, scaly and again does not fluoresce

questions.question: 196. A patient presents with papules which are greasy and brown over her chest. She is otherwise well. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 196... The answer is D. Dariers disease is an autosomal dominant condition characterized by abnormal keratinisation around hair follicles leading to greasy brown papules most often seen on chest and scapular. It is worsened by sun exposure There may be thickening of the palms and soles and nail changes.

questions.question: 197. What drug is most likely to cause a psoriatic type reaction?
questions.explanation: 197... The answer is D. The most likely culprit of psoriatic type reactions is beta blockers.Lupus type reactions, erythema multiforme and Stevens Johnson syndrome can be caused by antibiotics.

questions.question: 198. Psoriasis is associated with what HLA subtype?
questions.explanation: 198... The answer is E. Psoriasis is associated with HLA CW6 and HLA DR7. Pustular psoriasis and seronegative arthritis are associated with HLA B27. Rheumatoid Arthritis is associated with HLA DR3

questions.question: 199. A 25 year old female on the oral contraceptive has started to notice dark areas of pigmentation on her face. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 199... The answer is A. The most likely diagnosis is Chloasma which is a hormonally stimulated increase in melanogenesis. It mainly affects the face and it is seen most often in pregnancy and with COC due to the hormonal changes. Primary adrenal insufficiency can lead to hyperpigmentation but does not follow this pattern and is observed in mucous membranes. Acanthosis Nigricans is dark, thick velvety skin in skin creases and folds. It is associated with autoimmune disorders.

questions.question: 200. A 49-year-old male has noticed weak legs especially when standing up from a chair He also has noticed a rash on his knuckles and around his eyes. He is a heavy smoker. On examination her a purplish rash around his eyes and eyelids, some reddish papules on his knuckles and has proximal muscle weakness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 200... The answer is E. The most likely diagnosis is Dermatomyositis. The findings on the knuckles are Gottrons papules and the heliotrope rash around the eyes are characteristic.Nail fold haemorrhages are also seen. It is often associated with malignancy and in this case the gentleman should be investigated for an underlying malignancy especially as he is a heavy smoker. It also leads to a proximal muscle weakness. Steroids and azathioprine are useful in the management.

questions.question: 201. What is a feature of Squamous Cell Carcinoma?
options: B- Commonly metastasises to distant sites via venous spread
C- It is unusual but can metastasise via the lymphatics
E- Breslow thickness related to prognosis.
questions.explanation: 201... The answer is C. Squamous cell carcinomas usually occur on sun-exposed skin, or arise from Bowens Disease or chronic leg ulcer. It can metastasise via the lymphatics.Excision biopsy is required. Many patients have a recurrence but the prognosis is good.Breslow thickness and brown black color is related to Melanoma.
